ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Integrative Neuroscience
Concentration: 4+1 BS-MPH Program, 4+1 BS-MPA Program, 4+1 BS-MS HESA Program, 4+1 BS-MS SUST Program, 4+1 BS-MS Systems Science
Description: The integrative neuroscience major at Binghamton University offers students a strong foundation in biology, psychology, and chemistry, complemented by courses from various other disciplines.  This program is designed to provide the necessary breadth and depth for the interdisciplinary study of the biological bases of behavior.  Students are prepared for graduate studies in fields like neuroscience, anatomy, and physiology, as well as for professional schools such as medical or dental school.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematical Sciences
Concentration: mathematics, actuarial science, data science and statistics
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Mathematical Sciences program offers students a curriculum that balances theoretical foundations with practical problem-solving, preparing them for diverse applications in science, engineering, finance, and technology.  The program is designed to be more intensive than the BA, offering excellent preparation for students who wish to pursue graduate study in mathematics or a related field.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Concentration: 4+1 BS/MS Program
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering program provides a strong technical foundation in the broad field of mechanical engineering, accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET.  The curriculum emphasizes the application of engineering fundamentals with a balance of theory, design, and laboratory practice to prepare graduates for a creative, lifelong engineering career.  Students learn about thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, materials science, and robotics through hands-on projects and lab work.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nursing
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) program prepares students for a career as a registered professional nurse. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the sciences and humanities, combined with extensive clinical practice in diverse healthcare settings, to equip graduates to pass the National Council Licensure Examination (NCLEX-RN).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physics
Concentration: Physics, Applied Physics, Mathematical Physics
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Physics at Binghamton University provides students with rigorous training in the foundations of physics and mathematics. This program is designed to prepare students for graduate-level studies in physics, engineering, and other related disciplines, as well as for careers in applied sciences, research, and industry. The curriculum involves the study of matter, motion, and energy, applying scientific reasoning to understand reality from subatomic particles to the cosmos.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Social Work
Description: The Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) program at Binghamton University prepares students for generalist practice, focusing on understanding social work values, ethics, and professional behavior.  Through a generalist lens, students gain the knowledge and skills to work with individuals, families, groups, organizations, and communities, with a curriculum designed to link practice, policy, and research.  The program explores historical oppression and structural inequality, aiming to empower clients and communities.

ProgramName: Minor in Africana Studies
Concentration: History, PPL, Sociology, Literature, Music, Women's studies, Global public health, Religion
Description: The Minor in Africana Studies at Binghamton University provides students with a supplementary discipline to their primary major, focusing on the contributions and experiences of Africans and African-descended peoples worldwide.  The program is multidisciplinary, allowing students to explore topics from the perspectives of history, sociology, literature, music, and more, in consultation with faculty advisors.

ProgramName: Minor in Anthropology
Concentration: General Anthropology, Sociocultural Anthropology, Archaeology, Biological Anthropology, Linguistic Anthropology
Description: The General Anthropology minor provides students with a comprehensive background in the field of anthropology. It encourages the selection of courses from all subfields without requiring specialization in any single one.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Donor preferences, Program participation

ProgramName: Minor in Arabic Studies
Description: The Arabic minor focuses on developing proficiency in the Arabic language and understanding the literature and culture of the Arabic-speaking world. The curriculum requires a sequence of language courses, including Modern Standard Arabic, and allows for an additional related course. This program prepares students for careers in fields like business, foreign service, academics, and defense.

ProgramName: Minor in Art History
Description: The art history program at Binghamton University provides students with an understanding of the visual culture of humankind throughout history. The curriculum examines works of art as individual compositions of shape, space, and color, and as cultural artifacts with specific histories and functions within their societies. The program offers preparation for scholarly and professional work, including graduate study, museum and gallery positions, and careers in arts administration.

ProgramName: Minor in Art Studio
Concentration: Drawing, Painting, Sculpture, Printmaking, Photography, Graphic Design
Description: The Minor in Art and Design is for undergraduate students who want to supplement their studies with experience in studio art.  The curriculum provides a solid grounding in the creation, history, and theory of visual arts and design.  It consists of a minimum of six courses, totaling 24 credits, covering beginning, intermediate, and advanced levels in various studio areas.

ProgramName: Minor in Asian and Asian American Studies
Description: The minor in Asian and Asian American Studies (AAAS) allows students to supplement their major through participation in a cross-disciplinary program.  The program offers a comprehensive understanding of the histories, cultures, and societal contributions of Asian and Asian American communities, preparing students for careers that demand expertise in culture and language.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Program participation, Donor preference

ProgramName: Minor in Biological Sciences
Minor in Chemistry
Description: The Minor in Chemistry provides a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental concepts of chemistry, including both theoretical and practical components.  The program requires students to complete four chemistry courses (16 credits), with at least two being upper-level courses taken at Binghamton University.  Students will engage in coursework that enhances their skills and knowledge in the field.

ProgramName: Minor in Chinese
Description: The Chinese Studies minor at Binghamton University offers students a diverse curriculum focused on Chinese language, culture, and society. Its rigorous language curriculum emphasizes verbal and textual mastery and cultural competency.  Courses explore ancient and modern Chinese literature, visual arts, society, history, philosophy, and economics.

ProgramName: Minor in Cinema
Description: The Cinema minor at Binghamton University provides students with a foundation in the analytical and production skills of film and video. The program's primary focus is on how technical skills are utilized in the creation of meaningful artworks, with an emphasis on avant-garde, experimental, and documentary forms over commercial production.

ProgramName: Minor in Classical and Near Eastern Studies
Concentration: State, Self, and Social Power, Literature and Intellectual History, Religious Discourse, Authority, and Practice
Description: The minor in Classical and Near Eastern Religions and Cultures is an interdisciplinary program that provides a broad and in-depth appreciation for the complexities of ancient Mediterranean religion and culture. Students explore ancient literature, archaeological sites, artifacts, and manuscripts to learn about major historical figures, literature, and social realities. The program analyzes various ancient religions including Greek, Roman, ancient Israelite, Jewish, Christian, and Islam.

ProgramName: Minor in Comparative Literature
Description: The Minor in Comparative Literature allows students to explore literature across cultures, languages, and historical contexts. This interdisciplinary approach helps develop critical thinking and analytical skills through the study of various literary traditions. The program encourages cross-disciplinary work and offers great freedom for students to explore areas of their choice.

ProgramName: Minor in Computer Science
Concentration: Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity
Description: The Computer Science minor at Binghamton University helps students build skills in programming, algorithms, and software systems to complement majors in other fields.  Students will graduate with the ability to analyze complex computing problems and apply computer science theory and software development fundamentals to produce computing-based solutions.  The minor consists of seven courses that must be taken at Binghamton.

ProgramName: Minor in Creative Writing
Concentration: poetry, fiction, nonfiction, memoir, children's literature, screenwriting
Description: The Creative Writing Program at Binghamton University is designed to foster a powerful, disciplined, and skilled creativity within a supportive environment. Guided by internationally recognized faculty, the program prepares students for careers in a wide array of artistic and professional fields. Undergraduates pursue a BA in English with a creative writing specialization, which emphasizes critical thinking and personal voice.

ProgramName: Minor in Digital and Data Studies
Concentration: Data Science and Analytics, Web and Interactive Design, Digital Communication and Media, Digital Humanities, Global Public Health
Description: The Minor in Digital and Data Studies provides an interdisciplinary, hands-on immersion into digital literacy and data-inflected thinking. The curriculum integrates practice- and skills-based learning in programming, data analysis, computational processes, and web development with critical and scholarly study. The program aims to create knowledgeable consumers and engaged producers of digital content, promoting socially and culturally responsible approaches to technology.

ProgramName: Minor in Economics
Description: The Minor in Economics at Binghamton University provides students with a foundational background in economic concepts and analytical skills to complement their major field of study. The curriculum is designed to develop critical thinking for understanding economic institutions and issues in both contemporary and historical contexts. This background prepares students for a variety of paths, including graduate studies or careers in government, law, and business.

ProgramName: Minor in Education
Description: The Education Minor, taken in conjunction with an undergraduate student's major area of study, is designed to provide insight into careers in various educational fields as well as an appreciation for the role education plays in society. The minor provides a strong foundation for further work in education at the graduate level and provides pertinent information and experiences that expand the student's understanding of career opportunities. This program does not lead to New York State teaching certification.
ProgramCategory: Education##Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages

ProgramName: Minor in English
Description: The general English minor at Binghamton University encourages students to supplement their majors in other disciplines with a meaningful set of English courses.  The program consists of 6 total courses (24 credits) in English (ENG), Rhetoric (RHET), and/or Creative Writing (CW).  Students can tailor a program of study to fit their interests with guidance from departmental advisors.

ProgramName: Minor in Environmental Studies
Description: The Environmental Studies minor at Binghamton University allows students to explore a wide range of topics including climate change, conservation, environmental policy, and sustainable living. The program encourages engagement in fieldwork and projects, complementing any major by providing a deeper understanding of environmental issues. This minor aims to give students a competitive edge in the job market by developing valuable and sought-after skills.

ProgramName: Minor in Forensic Health
Description: The forensic health minor is open to any undergraduate at Binghamton University and is well suited for students majoring in fields with forensic applications such as nursing, biology, chemistry, and anthropology. This interdisciplinary program focuses on the application of health science to legal issues, preparing students for careers in healthcare, forensic sciences, or the law. The minor requires 24 credit hours, including core courses and adjunct courses.

ProgramName: Minor in French
Description: The Minor in French provides students with a strong foundation in French language comprehension, speaking, reading, and writing, as well as an understanding of the culture.  The program consists of six courses starting at the 211-level or above, with specific requirements for literature and upper-level coursework.  Students develop analytical, argumentative, and creative skills through various approaches that include written texts, film, and music.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Donor preferences, Program participation

ProgramName: Minor in Genocide and Mass Atrocity Prevention
Concentration: Historical and Contemporary Studies, Concepts and Theories, Practices and Methodologies
Description: The Minor in Genocide and Mass Atrocity Prevention (GMAP) provides students with an integrated set of courses to explore the historical, conceptual, and practical issues surrounding the prediction and prevention of mass atrocities.  This interdisciplinary program encourages students to study instances of genocide from various disciplinary approaches, understand the relevant political and legal concepts, and critically examine current prevention strategies.
ProgramCategory: Social Justice Studies##Conflict Resolution##History##Political Science##Sociology##Social Sciences##Ethnic Studies

ProgramName: Minor in Geography
Concentration: General Geography Minor, Geographical Information Systems Minor, Immigration/Migration Geography Minor, Physical Geography Minor, Environmental Resources Management Minor, Urban Planning Minor
Description: The Geography Department at Binghamton University empowers students to address contemporary problems such as physical resource development, racial/ethnic patterns, urban decay, business geography, and pollution. The curriculum helps students understand how natural and human environments are organized geographically by institutional decisions and human actions. The minor provides a foundation for careers in public and private planning agencies and other fields requiring spatial data analysis and resource management skills.

ProgramName: Minor in Geological Sciences
Concentration: Geology, Geophysics, Geochemistry
Description: The Minor in Geological Sciences is designed for students who have a general interest in the Earth sciences. The program requires 24 credits from the department's courses, providing a foundational understanding of Earth's processes, materials, and history.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Donor preferences, Program participation

ProgramName: Minor in German
Description: The Minor in German Studies at Binghamton University offers an interdisciplinary curriculum with a diverse range of courses in language, literature, and culture, emphasizing the study of culture in its broadest sense. The program is designed to develop proficiency in German, provide knowledge of the cultures of the German-speaking world, and foster cross-cultural competencies. Students can tailor their coursework to suit their interests, including topics from intellectual and cultural history to linguistics and visual culture.

ProgramName: Minor in Global Public Health
Description: The 24-credit undergraduate minor in Public Health uses a hands-on, active learning approach to expose students to the scientific foundations and core epidemiologic principles of public health. The minor is open to all undergraduate students and will augment many other undergraduate bachelor's degree programs. It is designed to be excellent preparation for various career paths, including those in health professions, social work, and law.

ProgramName: Minor in Health and Wellness Studies
Description: The Health and Wellness Studies minor provides a broad foundation in the concepts of health promotion and wellness education to encourage healthy living. Students evaluate scientific literature and research related to health, wellness and disease prevention. This knowledge is applied to assess, plan, motivate, and implement health-promoting behaviors and cultivate lifelong wellness for diverse populations.

ProgramName: Minor in History
Description: The Minor in History at Binghamton University is designed to encourage students to supplement their major in another discipline with a coherent program in history.  The program requires a minimum of six history courses (24 credit hours), with specific requirements for course levels and residency.  Students develop a program to satisfy the minor requirements in consultation with the department's advisors.

ProgramName: Minor in Human Development
Concentration: Immigration Studies
Description: The Human Development minor at Binghamton University allows students to explore the individual, social, and structural aspects of human development. The program focuses on understanding principles that benefit individuals and communities by examining social, cultural, economic, historical, and political frameworks.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Program participation, Donor preferences

ProgramName: Minor in Immigration Studies
Description: The interdisciplinary Minor in Immigration Studies explores the complex ways citizenship is defined and experienced at global, societal, and individual levels.  It focuses on how contemporary ideas of citizenship, translated into policy and practice, affect the lives of immigrants, refugees, and displaced people.  The program applies a social justice and rights-based philosophy to examine citizenship, immigration, and immigrant lives in various contexts.

ProgramName: Minor in International Studies
Description: The Global Studies Minor (GSM) is an innovative, multi-disciplinary program where students use experiential and cross-cultural learning to achieve an understanding of international, regional, and global issues. The minor is open to all undergraduate students who wish to add a formally recognized global dimension to their program of study. It is designed to enhance a student's major with a global component and expand future options based on acquired international knowledge and intercultural proficiency.

ProgramName: Minor in Italian
Minor in Japanese
Description: The Japanese Studies minor fosters detailed, nuanced knowledge and understanding of various aspects of premodern, modern and contemporary Japanese culture and society, including history, language, literature, and visual culture. It provides a solid foundation of Japanese language skills, including reading, writing, speaking and listening comprehension. The minor consists of six courses: three required language sequence courses and three required elective courses.

ProgramName: Minor in Judaic Studies
Concentration: Jewish communal service, Jewish history, Jewish thought, Holocaust studies, literature and culture
Description: The Judaic Studies minor at Binghamton University offers students an interdisciplinary perspective on three millennia of Jewish culture, including social, religious, and political history, as well as literature and thought.  The curriculum is drawn from both the humanities and social sciences, covering a wide array of topics.  This program prepares students for various careers and for graduate or professional studies by developing skills in cross-cultural adaptation, critical analysis, and logical communication.

ProgramName: Minor in Korean
Description: The Minor in Korean Studies provides students with a solid foundation in Korean language skills and knowledge of Korea's history, literature, and culture.  The program aims to enrich understanding of contemporary issues in Korea while enhancing critical thinking and analytical skills.  It consists of six courses, including required language courses and electives in areas like literature, history, and culture.

ProgramName: Minor in Latin American and Caribbean Studies
Description: The Latin American and Caribbean Studies (LACAS) minor offers an interdisciplinary and transnational approach to the study of Latin America, the Caribbean, and peoples of Latin American and Caribbean descent. It is designed for undergraduates who want formal recognition for coursework in the field without completing a full major. The program helps students build skills in research, critical thinking, and effective communication.

ProgramName: Minor in Leadership and Applied Social Science
Description: The Education Minor, taken with a student's major, provides insight into careers in various educational fields and an appreciation for the role education plays in society. It provides a strong foundation for graduate-level work in education and expands understanding of careers like classroom teaching, educational law, and administration. This minor does not lead to teacher certification.

ProgramName: Minor in Linguistics
Description: The linguistics minor at Binghamton University is an interdivisional program requiring six courses. It is designed to give students a foundation in the analysis of communicative behaviors through both scientific and cultural lenses. The curriculum emphasizes oral presentation, communication skills, logic, and analytical reasoning.

ProgramName: Minor in Management
Description: The State University of New York at Binghamton does not offer an undergraduate 'Minor in Management' or 'Minor in Business Administration'. The university's School of Management provides major programs in Business Administration and Accounting, and offers an Accounting Minor for non-management students.

ProgramName: Minor in Mathematical Sciences
Description: The Minor in Mathematical Sciences provides a flexible curriculum for students to explore various areas of mathematics, preparing them for diverse applications in science, engineering, finance, and technology.  The program requires the completion of at least 24 credits in upper-level mathematics courses, balancing theoretical foundations with practical problem-solving.

ProgramName: Minor in Medieval and Renaissance Studies
Minor in Music
Concentration: Musicology and Ethnomusicology, Theory and Musicianship, Performance
Description: The Music Minor at Binghamton University requires 29 credits, offering students a curriculum that emphasizes liberal arts courses in music theory, history, and ethnomusicology, as well as practical performance experience.  All performance courses are open by audition to any student, regardless of their major, and the program is designed to be flexible, often completed as part of a double major.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Donor preferences, Program participation

ProgramName: Minor in Philosophy
Description: The Philosophy minor at Binghamton University asks fundamental questions about the world, human life, knowledge, and morality. The program trains students in logic, critical reasoning, and a range of analytical skills that are valuable for careers in law, business, government, and more.

ProgramName: Minor in Physics
Description: The Minor in Physics at Binghamton University provides a firm foundation in the principles of physics. The curriculum is designed to develop analytical, laboratory, and reasoning skills, preparing students for various work environments or further graduate study.  To complete the minor, students must take introductory physics courses, a modern physics course, and three additional upper-level courses.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Program participation, Donor preferences

ProgramName: Minor in Political Science
Concentration: General Political Science, American Politics, Comparative Politics, International Relations
Description: The Minor in Political Science consists of six courses (24 credits) in the Political Science (PLSC) department. The program offers several specialized tracks, allowing students to focus their studies on specific areas within the discipline. To complete the minor, at least three of the required courses must be taken in residence at Binghamton University.

ProgramName: Minor in Psychology
Description: The undergraduate minor in Psychology at Binghamton University provides students with a foundational understanding of the science of human behavior, thought, and emotion. The curriculum is designed to introduce the scientific method and its application to psychological topics, preparing students for further study or careers in a variety of fields.

ProgramName: Minor in Russian and East European Studies
Description: Meant to complement a wide range of majors, the East European and Eurasian Studies minor teaches region-specific concepts and research tools, while supporting students in developing introductory-level knowledge in at least one of the region's many languages.  This knowledge will equip students to better address issues related to this area in their future careers, whether these be in law, business, science, government or non-profit work, health, or teaching.

ProgramName: Minor in Sociology
Description: The Sociology minor aims to understand the social changes taking place throughout the world and relate them to developments in the contemporary United States. The curriculum allows students to acquire skills to see the social world from a critical perspective. Students also develop analytical tools to understand political life, social movements, social conflicts, and issues of social justice.

ProgramName: Minor in Spanish
Description: The Minor in Spanish is designed to develop language proficiency and cultural appreciation in Spanish-speaking regions. The program consists of six courses starting at the intermediate level or above, with a focus on literature and advanced studies. This minor provides students with linguistic and cultural competency, allowing them to communicate effectively with Latinos and Hispanics in the U.S. and their home countries.

ProgramName: Minor in Speech and Hearing Science
Description: The Division of Speech and Language Pathology (SLP) offers an undergraduate minor in speech and hearing science, which provides students with the basis necessary to develop foundational knowledge in normal and abnormal processes of speech, language and swallowing.  Completing this minor will not allow students to practice as speech-language pathologists but will prepare them to apply to a graduate program in the field.

ProgramName: Minor in Theatre
Description: The Minor in Theatre at Binghamton University provides students with a comprehensive exploration of performance, production, and dramatic theory.  The program focuses on developing skills in acting, directing, design, and stage management, alongside an understanding of the historical and cultural contexts of theatre.  Students gain practical, hands-on experience through participation in department productions, including plays, musicals, and dance performances.
ProgramCategory: Theater Arts##Performing Arts##Visual and Performing Arts
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Donor preference, Program participation

ProgramName: Minor in Translation
Description: The Minor in Translation Studies at Binghamton University is designed for students with advanced language skills who wish to demonstrate their commitment to translation, either as a potential career path or as an area of academic research.

ProgramName: Minor in Women, Gender and Sexuality Studies
Concentration: WGSS Minor, LGBT and Sexuality Studies Minor
Description: The Minor in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies at Binghamton University provides an interdisciplinary analysis of how gender and sexuality intersect with other identity markers like race, class, and legal status. Students in the program critically examine these dynamics to understand social inequalities and movements for change. The minor is designed to complement a wide range of majors, from STEM fields to the arts and humanities.
